title: Algorithms: introductory lesson

sources.coverage: Slides 2–35; lecture material on problem types, algorithms, program-development life cycle, properties, input/process/output, constructs, and worked examples.
Lesson 1 of 3; includes explanatory material, runnable Python examples, and practice on sequencing, selection, loops, tracing, sentinel input, digit reversal, and algorithm quality.

objectives.source: PDF slides 2–4, 10–12; algo.md sections ‘Two kinds of problems’, ‘Where the word comes from’, and ‘You already write algorithms every day’.
operations: classify an algorithmic versus heuristic problem
interpret an algorithm as ordered instructions
infer why order or exact instructions matter

objectives.source: PDF slides 5–9 and 16–17; algo.md ‘The three questions every algorithm answers’.
operations: distinguish analysis, design, coding, testing, and debugging
identify input, processing, and output from a scenario
choose the next development step

objectives.source: PDF slides 12–15; algo.md ‘What makes an algorithm a good algorithm’.
operations: diagnose finiteness, definiteness, effectiveness, input/output, and generality
compare supported algorithm-choice criteria
distinguish correctness from efficiency

objectives.source: PDF slides 17–21; algo.md ‘Construct 1 — Sequence’ and its average, interest, and rectangle examples.
operations: classify straight-line sequence
trace or correct arithmetic steps
map a formula task to inputs, processing, and outputs
trace conditional branches
maintain a largest-so-far value
reason about ties and comparison coverage

objectives.source: PDF slides 28–35; algo.md ‘Construct 3 — Iteration’, ‘The four parts of every loop’, and examples 6–9.
operations: select for versus while based on known repetition count
identify initialization, condition, body, and update
trace factorial and sentinel loops
interpret modulus and floor division in digit reversal

objectives.source: PDF slides 12–15 and 27; algo.md ‘The three-student scenario from the lecture’.
operations: compare alternative algorithms by stated criteria
judge efficiency as input size grows
identify hard-coded solutions that fail generality

excluded: Flowchart symbol memorization and detailed flowchart drawing; covered in the separate flowcharts lecture, not this requested source pair.
Python topics beyond the examples in algo.md, including lists, functions, data structures, asymptotic notation, and sorting implementations.
Historical claims about al-Khwarizmi beyond the modest attribution printed in the PDF; the web lesson makes additional claims that are not independently supported by the lecture source.
bloomPolicy: Bloom classification is descriptive review evidence, not a quota. Create is not assigned to single-select MCQs.
